intro.markdown:
Five `promptctl/links-issue-tracker` releases went out today — 0.11.0 through 0.12.3, one every couple of hours, ending with the tag that closed the release-ci epic. The final promotion was itself the first live exercise of the pipeline that ships it. Brandon did not stop to celebrate; the next commit split the DDL-text parsing toolkit out of `migration_runner.go`.

The shape I keep seeing is a fix per verb. `promptctl/crom` added `restart` and `show` and then filed five separate pull requests behind them — one to hold the profile lock across the whole rotation, one to stop the browser a failed launch had already started, one to report `osascript`'s exit status when it says nothing else, one to make a stop mean the port is free rather than the process table is empty. Each PR carried the argument for why the previous version was silently wrong.

`brandon-fryslie/rich-js` fixed a width bug twice — once for `Panel`, once for `Table` — and then extended the fix to a suite that sweeps every renderable across the widths nobody was testing. That is the sequence I would recognise as Brandon's if I saw it on a strange repo.

`RenderCache` publishes reload completion so tests await it ([#199](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/199)); `install` warns loudly on a stale staged version ([#201](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/201)). ### [elvenspeak](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak) **Python** Serves the ElevenLabs text-to-speech API from a local engine. 31 commits over the past 90 days — a brand-new repo initialized this week. `speech.py` split at the "and" in its purpose sentence ([#3](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/3)); the engine interface defined from what the endpoints need ([#4](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/4)) and made a suite every engine passes ([#8](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/8)); the environment chooses the engine so build and boot cannot disagree ([#9](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/9)); a second engine added ([#10](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/10)); one image per engine built in CI from a commit no working tree touched ([#13](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/13)); each engine gets its own alias table with voices baked ([#14](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/14)); `GET /v1/models` answers with the engine this image was built with ([#18](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/18)); a remote elvenspeak becomes a discovered engine ([#20](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/20)); Spanish spoken in Spanish ([#32](https://github.com/promptctl/elvenspeak/pull/32)).
